inputs.delta_definition: ae(N) - ae(R) on best checkpoints; positive => R better

A1_coverage.note: cells are a complete partition of the 1000 valid rows across tier x side x size_novel x sig_novel; empty cells are omitted

A3_n_multi.premise: n_multi == 1 (and n_multi == 0) molecules have identical R and S block content, so they are the input-equivalence negative control for the R-vs-S comparison

S1_conservation.note: relative error is ~1e-15 in float64 (v1 C3); this is the fp32 path

S4_gradient.note: v1's mechanism gate is 'block grad at step 1 > 1e-8'; step 0 is zero by the zero-initialised reader_ext and is expected to be 0

S5_prediction_consistency.note: on n_multi<=1 the S content is identical to R, so a frozen model must produce identical predictions; N differs there too because N also replaces singleton content

A5_probe.claim_limit: fixed-weight content substitution measures what the trained network reads. It is not a causal estimate of generalization: the weights were fit on one content construction, so an off-distribution substitution conflates 'reads this' with 'was trained for this'.
